text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn told Socialist Party executives that unjustified disputes within the party are harming its prestige, and encouraged them to co-ordinate their position on individual issues. @
- A National Bank official denied on Friday that large sums of forged banknotes from imported paper are in wide circulation.
- The Meat Industry Workers' Union will stage a demonstration outside Parliament today.
- Farmers blocked roads in a number of villages in the Hungarian Plain on Friday to protest against recent tax and social insurance regulations. (Sat.)
- Young Democrat president Viktor Orban heavily criticised the government's economic policy on Saturday. @
- The Christian Democratic Party's national board Saturday modified the party statute by expanding its own powers and those wielded by the party president.
- Hungary was one of 68 signatories to the World Trade Organisation's global telecoms liberalisation agreement in Geneva on the weekend.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny said the cabinet supports the compromise formulas for pension reform and expects to decide on a draft bill in two or three weeks. Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha said at least 30 percent of the shares of the truck manufacturer Raba will be offered for sale. (Sat.)
NEPSZABADSAG
- Young Democrat Tamas Deutsch soared to second place, while Prime Minister Gyula Horn lost five points and is in the 25th place, according to the latest popularity poll.
MAGYAR NEMZET @
- Romanian Defence Minister Victor Babiuc is due to visit Hungary today.
- Political state secretaries from Italy, Slovenia and Hungary agreed in Rome on Friday that the prime ministers of the three countries will meet in Budapest in May.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- This paper today produces a chart showing the economic forecasts for Hungary in the next two years, as made by 12 private economic and financial institutions by 12 private economic and financial institutions surveyed by Reuters. @
- The Hungarian Oil and Gas Co. MOL reported consolidated business profits of HUF 26.6 billion.
- Consumers saved a total net HUF 33.3 billion in January, down from HUF 41 billion in January 1996.
- Output in the civil engineering industry fell by 1.1 percent last year compared to 1995, the Central Statistics Office reports.
- The chemical company TVK recorded pre-tax profits of HUF 8.75 billion last year. (Sat.)
- BorsodChem Rt.'s 1996 balance sheet shows pre-tax profits of HUF 7.2 billion. (Sat.) @
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Budapest Bank, Realbank and Postabank closed 1996 with profits, according to preliminary results.
- Last week the cabinet approved a proposal allowing foreign-based banks to open branch offices in Hungary from January 1, 1998.
- Tile-maker Zalakeramia reported a pre-tax profit of HUF 1.48 billion for last year.
- The State Insurance Supervision has issued a license for the Austrian insurance Company Grawe to operate in Hungary.
